title: Build a Two-Tower Recommender
blurb: Build the retrieval stage of a recommender: two towers, in-batch negatives, the logQ correction, top-K retrieval and recall, tail recall and coverage.
intro: Large recommenders first retrieve a few hundred candidates from millions of items, and two-tower models are the standard way to do it: one network for users, one for items, scored by a dot product. The steps score every user against every item, train with the other items in a batch as negatives, correct the bias that sampling puts on popular items, retrieve the top items a user has not seen, and judge the lists by recall, tail recall and coverage. The capstone trains normalised linear towers with in-batch negatives, with and without the correction, and evaluates full-catalogue retrieval.
